nodes.label: P2P Client Port Contract
nodes.rationale: Behavior contract for removing the server from live play. It records what the backend does today, as implemented and as locked by tests. Server transport does not move. The rules, lobby state machine, and message meanings do.

nodes.label: Server Transport
nodes.rationale: HTTP, STOMP, PostgreSQL, and session-token hashing stay behind. They are transport, not rules, so they are not part of the peer port.

nodes.label: Leaders P2P Client
nodes.rationale: The client that implements this contract is the Leaders game inside one Next.js app. Other games do not import Leaders lobby or rules. They share only common/.

nodes.label: openMesh
nodes.rationale: openMesh takes an app id, a room code, handshake and relay timeouts, and two channel names. Leaders uses app id app.dirigeant, request channel lobby-intent, and broadcast channel lobby-feed. Handshake payload, host authority, and game commands stay in the Leaders connection module so the mesh is not Leaders-specific.

nodes.label: room-connection.ts
nodes.rationale: Leaders lobby, seats, chat, and commands live here, including host authority, so game policy is not pushed into common/p2p.

nodes.label: leaders/domain
nodes.rationale: The Leaders rules engine lives under leaders/domain/. Tests live next to those files as *.test.ts.

nodes.label: leaders/app
nodes.rationale: Play and room screens live in leaders/app/ and are served at /game/leaders.

nodes.label: Engine and Tests Win
nodes.rationale: When this file and the design note disagree, the engine and the tests win. The design note describes the board game; the engine is what ships, so the port follows implemented behavior. Disagreements include archer visibility, frog duration, claw drag distance, hermit hand counting, cub placement, no leader-type choice, vizier step shape, frog path, brewmaster moving the leader, illusionist ally swaps, first-sniper-only, single skipped recruitment phase, empty legalActions during recruitment, and the tactician block omitted from GameStateView.

nodes.label: Project Design Note
nodes.rationale: The note at .cursor/rules/project-specific-guidelines.mdc describes the board game. It is not the source of truth when it disagrees with the engine.

nodes.label: Infrastructure Kept Off the Client
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL, Flyway, JDBC, actuator health, Swagger, CORS, the /app/echo demo, the STOMP broker, and SHA-256 storage of seat tokens stay out of the game client.

nodes.label: Peer-Owned Concerns
nodes.rationale: Each peer must own lobby, presence, chat, match setup, rules, and agreement. Agreement means one shared state, a monotonic version, and identical resolution on both peers. Peers need a shared initial state or a shared seed plus an identical shuffle, because a solo shuffle diverges the match.

nodes.label: GameStateFactory
nodes.rationale: GameStateFactory uses java.util.Random with no seed. Piece ids, the game id, and the deck order are random. If each client shuffles alone, the matches diverge, so opening randomness must be agreed once before the first command.

nodes.label: Fixed Host and Guest Colors
nodes.rationale: Colors are fixed at start, not random, so both peers can derive seats without a color lottery. Host player id is BLACK on crown cell 36 (q=0, r=3). Guest player id is WHITE on crown cell 0 (q=0, r=-3).

nodes.label: RoomLobbyQueryAdapter
nodes.rationale: toLobby maps host to blackPlayerId and guest to whitePlayerId, which is how lobby seats become the fixed colors.

nodes.label: Lobby
nodes.rationale: The lobby must move peer-to-peer: create, join, leave, ready, roles, unique names, and room status.

nodes.label: Username Validation
nodes.rationale: The whole string is case-sensitive and must match [a-zA-Z0-9_]{3,64}. Names are unique inside one room and may repeat in another. Losing a seat secret does not reclaim the username: a new join is a new player id, and the old name still blocks.

nodes.label: Invite Code
nodes.rationale: Default length is 6, allowed range 4-12. The alphabet omits I, O, 0, and 1 so codes stay readable. Lookup trims and uppercases. Generation tries at most 10 times, then fails if it cannot find a unique code.

nodes.label: Lobby Roles
nodes.rationale: Roles are HOST, GUEST, and SPECTATOR. At most one host, the creator. At most one guest. Everyone else is a spectator. Members are ordered by join time.

nodes.label: Room Status
nodes.rationale: Status moves WAITING to LOBBY to IN_GAME to FINISHED. Create starts WAITING with the creator as HOST and ready false, and publishes no presence event. A command that sets GameStatus.WON sets the room to FINISHED. Host leave is rejected and the seat stays.

nodes.label: JoinRoom
nodes.rationale: JoinRoom does not read the current status. If the guest slot is empty, the joiner becomes guest and the room is set to LOBBY even when it was IN_GAME, so a game record can still exist beside that lobby. A join while a guest exists is a spectator and does not change status or publish presence.

nodes.label: Ready
nodes.rationale: Only HOST or GUEST may ready, and only while status is LOBBY. Ready is not on the member list; clients learn it only from presence, so a roster snapshot cannot show it. One ready player does not start the game. Both ready starts the match, publishes GAME_STARTED, then the initial game state. The start response includes the game destination and does not repeat the seat secret. A second start throws Game already started.

nodes.label: Disconnect
nodes.rationale: Disconnect handling applies only to rooms where that connection subscribed to presence. In IN_GAME the seat is kept and only DISCONNECTED is published, so a drop does not free a match seat. In LOBBY or WAITING a guest fully leaves, a spectator is removed, and a host cannot be removed. FINISHED is treated like lobby, and the host still cannot be removed.

nodes.label: Presence
nodes.rationale: Payload fields are type, playerId, username, and role. Subscribing emits PLAYER_CONNECTED or SPECTATOR_CONNECTED again with no dedup, so clients must tolerate repeats. GAME_STARTED uses the player id, name, and role of the ready call that completed the pair. There is no spectator-left type; spectator leave uses DISCONNECTED.

nodes.label: Chat
nodes.rationale: Player chat is sent by host and guest and read by every member. Spectator chat is spectators only in both directions, which keeps table talk off the player channel. Empty text is rejected. There is no maximum length. Chat is not stored, so late joiners do not receive history. There are no chat unit tests; the rules come from the send use case, the command, and the STOMP interceptor.

nodes.label: Game Traffic Permissions
nodes.rationale: Only a host or guest may submit a command, and only while the room is IN_GAME. Any member may request a snapshot; if no game exists the request is ignored. Any member may read game state. On subscribe, if a game exists, that subscriber receives the current GameStateView once.

nodes.label: Shared Game State
nodes.rationale: Both peers store the same fields so resolution can be identical. version starts at 0 and increases by 1 after every accepted command. status is IN_PROGRESS or WON. activeColor is whose turn it is except during Nemesis. firstPlayerColor is the random starter and is used only for second-player compensation. activeAbilityBlockedThisPhase must be kept locally because the wire view omits it.

nodes.label: PendingAbility
nodes.rationale: Multi-step abilities stay pending so a partial Acrobat, Royal Guard, Vizier, or Manipulator step can be finished or abandoned. Ending the action phase clears the pending ability and marks that piece acted.

nodes.label: GameStateView
nodes.rationale: Camel-case JSON. Enums use Java names. Piece and player ids are UUID strings. Cell ids are numbers and cellToPiece keys are decimal strings. activeAbilityBlockedThisPhase is stored and used by the engine but omitted from the view, so a client that only mirrors the broadcast forgets Tactician's block. The port must keep the field. legalActions is computed for the current actor and sent to every subscriber, including spectators.

nodes.label: GameLegalAction
nodes.rationale: legalActions is an empty list outside ACTION and when the game is WON. END_ACTION_PHASE and RECRUIT are valid commands but are never listed, so the client builds those two itself.

nodes.label: Game Command
nodes.rationale: Types are DEFAULT_MOVE, ACTIVE_ABILITY, END_ACTION_PHASE, and RECRUIT. If actionKey is non-blank it is decoded and the other command fields are ignored, so the key is the authority. expectedVersion must equal the current version or the rejection is STALE_VERSION and state does not change. A lost race on save uses Concurrent game update with the same code. Rejected commands never mutate state.

nodes.label: actionKey
nodes.rationale: UTF-8 payload, Base64 URL without padding, prefix v1. A legacy Royal Guard secondCellId is not copied onto targetCellId, so the view still shows the first cell. choiceGroup is CLAW:targetPieceId when params contain both mode and targetPieceId.

nodes.label: Opening State
nodes.rationale: createInitial then beginTurnIfNeeded. There is no leader-type choice: selected_leader exists in an old migration and is unused, and both players always receive LEADER. The deck is every CharacterType except LEADER, shuffled, 21 cards. HERMIT and CUB are both in the deck, and Hermit's recruit also places an extra cub, so two cubs can exist. activeColor and firstPlayerColor are the same random color.

nodes.label: Board Topology
nodes.rationale: 37 axial cells, ids 0..36, row lengths 4, 5, 6, 7, 6, 5, 4. Six neighbor directions in a fixed order. Crown cells have 3 neighbors, not 6. Surround checks actual neighbors, so a leader still on its crown is surrounded when those 3 cells are occupied. Crowns are not recruitment cells.

nodes.label: Recruitment Zones
nodes.rationale: WHITE recruitment is cells 1, 2, 3, 4, 9, and 15. BLACK recruitment is cells 33, 34, 35, 32, 27, and 21. Other border cells are in neither zone.

nodes.label: Turn Machine
nodes.rationale: apply refuses anything when status is not IN_PROGRESS. If resolvingNemesis is true, only Nemesis resolution handles the command and the active-color check is skipped. Otherwise the actor must equal activeColor.

nodes.label: GameRulesEngine
nodes.rationale: Legal-action candidates are simulated with apply. Anything that throws is dropped, so the published list is exactly the moves the engine will accept.

nodes.label: Action Phase
nodes.rationale: Each of the active player's pieces may complete at most one action, in any order. Ending early skips the rest. Frog move is any empty cell at hex distance 1 or 2, not only a straight line, and the path may be occupied. The written note's straight-line wording is not what the engine does. Frog does not disable the default move. allowsDefaultMove is false for NEMESIS and WILL_O_THE_WISP. The message Frog already acted is unreachable because actedThisPhase throws first.

nodes.label: End Action Phase
nodes.rationale: END_ACTION_PHASE clears acted, ability-blocked, and pending, then sets RECRUITMENT. If the hand has at least 5 cards or no offer is legally placeable, it consumes one recruitment phase and does not loop. A second phase with a full hand or no legal offer has no skip command, unlike the written note's skip-recruitment wording. A full hand in that leftover phase makes RECRUIT throw Hand full.

nodes.label: Recruit
nodes.rationale: RECRUIT requires RECRUITMENT, an offer index, and an empty cell in that player's zone. The leader card counts toward the hand limit of 5. Offers refill from the front of the deck and may stay below 3. An offer is legal when at least one empty zone cell exists. For HERMIT, canRecruitOffer also requires fewer than 4 non-leader cards before the recruit and an empty recruitment neighbor for the cub.

nodes.label: Second-Player Compensation
nodes.rationale: The next player gets two recruitment phases only when nextTurn is 2 and nextColor is not firstPlayerColor. That is the second player's first turn only. The first player always has one.

nodes.label: End of Full Turn
nodes.rationale: Leader safety runs before the opponent-capture win check, so a player cannot finish a turn that leaves their own leader unsafe in order to capture the opponent. Sniper is not checked mid-turn. Capture and surround of the opponent are not checked mid-action. applyRecruit calls finishRecruitmentPhase first and, if that returns WON, skips the post-recruit leader-safety comparison. If a recruit does not win, safety compares the pre-recruit state to the state after the phase advance: an already-unsafe leader does not freeze later moves.

nodes.label: Sniper Win
nodes.rationale: At the start of the sniper owner's turn, that player wins when they have a SNIPER and the enemy leader is on the same straight line at distance 3 or more. Visibility is not required. Distance 2 does not win. Only the first sniper of that color in piece-map order is inspected.

nodes.label: Capture
nodes.rationale: A missing leader counts as captured. Two or more enemy captors capture the leader. An adjacent enemy ASSASSIN captures with no second captor. Frogged pieces, WILL_O_THE_WISP, and CUB do not count. An archer counts only when not adjacent, on the same straight line, at distance exactly 2, and visible. The written note allowed an archer to help when not visible; the engine does not. An adjacent archer is not a standard neighbor captor either.

nodes.label: Surround
nodes.rationale: Every neighbor cell of the leader must be occupied. Owner and type do not matter. One empty neighbor prevents it. A missing leader counts as surrounded.

nodes.label: After Nemesis
nodes.rationale: Both leaders are checked, active player first. If both are down, the opponent wins because the active leader is checked first. Nemesis skips leader safety, which is the only time a player may complete a move that newly endangers their own leader.

nodes.label: Global Ability Gates
nodes.rationale: Gates run before a character's own active ability. Jailor blocks active abilities only; default moves still work, and a friendly jailor does not block. Protector blocks an enemy ability that moves an enemy piece when the target is an enemy PROTECTOR or a friendly PROTECTOR of that target is adjacent. Same-owner targets are not protected, so Illusionist may swap an ally. Protector does not block default moves, self-moves, Shaman's frog, or Tactician and Brewmaster moving their own ally.

nodes.label: IllegalGameMoveException
nodes.rationale: Rules rejections surface as ILLEGAL_MOVE with this exception's message. The client should keep those strings if it surfaces the same errors.

nodes.label: Leader
nodes.rationale: Default move only, unless Vizier applies. There is no leader-type selection. With Vizier, a one-step move opens a pending adjacent step, and a single command may also land on an empty distance-2 cell through an empty midpoint that need not be collinear. The written note described only one additional empty step. Any leader move, including the first hex of a Vizier step, can start Nemesis. apply checks resolvingNemesis before pending abilities, so the pending Vizier step remains. Leader safety runs on both steps.

nodes.label: Shaman
nodes.rationale: Frogs an enemy non-leader on a visible straight line. The flag is stored as turnNumber+1 and cleared when the turn counter reaches that value, which is the start of the opponent's turn. The written note said the frog lasts through the opponent's full turn. No test covers the timer. A frog never counts as a captor.

nodes.label: Sniper
nodes.rationale: Passive only. Default move. The win is checked at the start of the owner's turn, and a second sniper is ignored.

nodes.label: Tactician
nodes.rationale: Requires some ally adjacent to the enemy leader, then moves a different or same non-leader ally one step. That ally is ability-blocked for the rest of the action phase but can still default-move. The block is omitted from GameStateView, so the port must store it locally or the ally could act again.

nodes.label: Will o' the Wisp
nodes.rationale: No default move. Teleports to any empty cell, including cells adjacent to enemies. Never a captor, even when not a frog.

nodes.label: Acrobat
nodes.rationale: Up to two jumps over an occupied adjacent cell, plus a normal default move if chosen instead. If a second jump exists, the first jump stays pending and does not mark acted, so the piece can still take the second jump. While pending, legalActions contains only second-jump targets and the complete action. The first-step view carries targetPieceId and a null targetCellId.

nodes.label: Rider
nodes.rationale: Moves to distance exactly 2 on a straight line. Every cell on that line except the origin must be empty, including the destination.

nodes.label: Bruiser
nodes.rationale: Pushes an adjacent enemy onto one of at most three opposite hexes, excluding the bruiser's own side, then steps onto the enemy's old cell. Protector is checked on the enemy. A border enemy can have fewer than three pushes. Both pieces stay in cellToPiece.

nodes.label: Royal Guard
nodes.rationale: The guard may start anywhere. The first step must be an empty neighbor of the leader, not necessarily of the guard. A legacy numeric secondCellId still resolves both steps at once, but the legal-action view exposes only the first cell. The optional second step excludes the leader's cell.

nodes.label: Illusionist
nodes.rationale: Swaps with a visible non-adjacent enemy or ally, not itself. The written note did not spell out ally swaps. Protector applies only to enemy targets.

nodes.label: Claw Launcher
nodes.rationale: Advance moves the claw to the cell immediately before the target. Drag moves the target the full distance to the cell next to the claw in one action, not a one-step nudge; the path between must be empty. Protector applies to drag. choiceGroup is CLAW:targetPieceId.

nodes.label: Manipulator
nodes.rationale: Two steps, enemy only. Step 1 selects a visible non-adjacent enemy and does not move yet. Step 2 moves that piece one cell toward or away along the line. A single command that already includes targetCellId skips the pending state. Protector applies.

nodes.label: Wanderer
nodes.rationale: Teleports to any empty cell that is not adjacent to an enemy. Adjacent to allies is allowed. Jailor and leader safety still apply, so the teleport is not an escape from those gates.

nodes.label: Brewmaster
nodes.rationale: Moves an adjacent ally one empty step, and that ally may be the leader. The written note said an adjacent ally without calling out the leader. The ally is not marked acted and is not ability-blocked.

nodes.label: Archer
nodes.rationale: Passive. Default move only. Capture help requires visibility at distance exactly 2 and not adjacent. An adjacent archer never helps.

nodes.label: Assassin
nodes.rationale: Passive. Default move only. Adjacent to the enemy leader, the assassin captures alone. That check is at end of turn and after Nemesis, not mid-action.

nodes.label: Jailor
nodes.rationale: Passive. Default move only. An enemy jailor on a neighbor cell blocks active abilities and does not block default moves.

nodes.label: Protector
nodes.rationale: Passive. Default move only. Blocks enemy abilities that move an enemy piece onto or adjacent to a protector. Does not protect same-owner targets.

nodes.label: Vizier
nodes.rationale: Passive. Default move only. In play means the VIZIER card is in the hand or a vizier piece of that color is on the board. The effect is on the leader, not on the vizier piece.

nodes.label: Nemesis
nodes.rationale: No voluntary action during its owner's action phase. When the enemy leader's cell changes and a legal landing exists, resolvingNemesis becomes true. Only the Nemesis owner may move, only with a distance-2 straight clear-path move, the same geometry as Rider. activeColor does not change. Leader safety is skipped. If no landing is legal, resolution does not start.

nodes.label: Hermit
nodes.rationale: Passive on the board. Recruiting the hermit also places a cub on the first empty same-zone neighbor in direction order; the player does not choose that cell. canRecruitOffer allows 3 non-leaders before the recruit, but recruitCubPair counts after the hermit is added and rejects 4 or more, so a successful recruit needs at most 2 non-leaders beforehand. The written note said fewer than 4 non-leader cards. If hermit is the only face-up card in the illegal state, ending the action phase will not skip recruitment and RECRUIT will throw.

nodes.label: Cub
nodes.rationale: Passive. Default move only. Never captures. One cub is in the deck and another can be placed by a hermit recruit, so two cubs can exist. On the board, hermit and cub each get their own action.

nodes.label: Legal Actions
nodes.rationale: Computed only when status is IN_PROGRESS and phase is ACTION. Nemesis resolution and a pending ability short-circuit the catalog. Otherwise each unacted piece of the active player contributes default moves and, unless frogged, tactician-blocked, or jailor-adjacent, its actives. legalActions is empty during RECRUITMENT, so the client must know RECRUIT and END_ACTION_PHASE on its own. The written note said the player chooses a legal face-up card from the legal-move list.

nodes.label: LegalActionsResolver
nodes.rationale: The view's legalActions must match LegalActionsResolver for that state, so spectators and both players see the same actor's list.

nodes.label: Rejection Message Catalog
nodes.rationale: These strings are the ILLEGAL_MOVE message. The client should keep them if it surfaces the same errors, so peer rejections stay recognizable. STALE_VERSION covers both Stale game version and Concurrent game update.

nodes.label: Peer Consensus
nodes.rationale: The server is the only writer of game state today. Two clients must pick one authority model and keep the invariants: same command and same version yield the same next state, including generated piece ids; a wrong version is ignored and the sender is told the real version; a rejection does not bump the version or broadcast; an accept bumps by 1 and every member, including spectators, sees the same view.

nodes.label: SubmitGameCommandUseCase
nodes.rationale: Loads state, checks expectedVersion, runs apply, and on WON marks the room finished, then saves version expectedVersion+1 and broadcasts the new view. That single-writer path is what peers have to replace.

nodes.label: Move Log
nodes.rationale: Each accepted command is appended with the new version, the acting player id, and the command payload. The log is not required to play, but it is the current audit trail.

nodes.label: Port Test Checklist
nodes.rationale: Port tests should keep these names' assertions. Paths are under src/test/java/org/luyys/template/. The names are the lock on behavior, not just examples.

nodes.label: leaders/domain/game-state.ts
nodes.rationale: Must include activeAbilityBlockedThisPhase even though GameStateView omits it.

nodes.label: leaders/domain/abilities.ts
nodes.rationale: One function per character, plus the four pending ability ids.

nodes.label: leaders/domain/legal-actions.ts
nodes.rationale: Simulates apply and omits recruit and end-phase, matching the server catalog.

nodes.label: leaders/domain/submit.ts
nodes.rationale: Version check, broadcast-on-accept, and identical ids for recruited pieces. The host path also lives in room-connection.ts.

nodes.label: common/p2p
nodes.rationale: Shared mesh for signaling, ICE, request, and broadcast. Game rules do not live here.

nodes.label: CreateRoomUseCaseTests
nodes.rationale: Locks that a new room is WAITING, the creator is HOST, and the raw token is not what is stored.

nodes.label: JoinRoomUseCaseTests
nodes.rationale: Locks guest versus spectator assignment, duplicate usernames, unknown codes, GUEST_JOINED payload, and roster contents.

nodes.label: LeaveRoomUseCaseTests
nodes.rationale: Locks guest leave back to WAITING, spectator leave without a status change, host cannot leave, and missing member or room.

nodes.label: SetPlayerReadyUseCaseTests
nodes.rationale: Locks ready and unready presence events and that one ready player does not start the game.

nodes.label: RoomControllerTests
nodes.rationale: Locks the full role flow, guest-slot reuse, roster growth, unknown join, and that ready requires the seat secret without echoing it.

nodes.label: RoomDisconnectListenerTest
nodes.rationale: Locks that an in-game drop keeps the seat and a lobby drop removes the guest.

nodes.label: RoomStompChannelInterceptorTest
nodes.rationale: Locks game-topic subscribe, the private rejection channel, and snapshot requests including the app-prefixed destination.

nodes.label: RoomDestinationsTest
nodes.rationale: Locks that only broker topics count as room subscriptions and that the channel name is the segment after the room code.

nodes.label: BoardTopologyTests
nodes.rationale: Locks 37 cells, the two recruitment zone id sets, and that crowns and other border cells are excluded.

nodes.label: CaptureEvaluatorTest
nodes.rationale: Locks two-captor capture, cub/wisp/frog exclusions, assassin, archer visibility, surround, and sniper distance.

nodes.label: GameRulesEngineWinTest
nodes.rationale: Locks that capture and surround win at phase end, sniper wins at turn start, and a winning recruit returns WON without the leader-safety throw.

nodes.label: GameRulesEngineTests
nodes.rationale: Locks rejection of a move when it is not that player's turn.

nodes.label: NemesisResolutionTest
nodes.rationale: Locks that only the Nemesis owner moves, activeColor stays, and the active player is blocked until resolution.

nodes.label: LegalActionsResolverTest
nodes.rationale: Locks that a fresh game lists leader default moves.

nodes.label: LegalActionsResolverEdgeCasesTest
nodes.rationale: Locks tactician pin versus move, frogged pieces losing actives, wisp teleport only, protector blocking manipulator, and pending acrobat freezing other pieces.

nodes.label: CharacterLegalActionsTest
nodes.rationale: Locks the legal-action shape of each character, including passives that default-move only and Nemesis having no voluntary action.

nodes.label: WandererLegalActionsTest
nodes.rationale: Locks non-enemy-adjacent destinations, jailor suppression, and both leader-safety cases: already unsafe still allows the teleport, newly unsafe rejects it.

nodes.label: AcrobatLegalActionsTest
nodes.rationale: Locks that step 1 and step 2 name the jumped piece and do not carry a cell.

nodes.label: ManipulatorLegalActionsTest
nodes.rationale: Locks piece-only step 1, cell step 2, hidden enemies behind a closer piece, and exclusion of adjacent enemies.

nodes.label: RoyalGuardLegalActionsTest
nodes.rationale: Locks leader-adjacent first steps from anywhere, pending second step or complete, and legacy secondCellId.

nodes.label: VizierLeaderMoveLegalActionsTest
nodes.rationale: Locks vizier destinations, adjacent-only pending steps, and that either vizier shape ends the leader's action.

nodes.label: BruiserPushLegalActionsTest
nodes.rationale: Locks push geometry, empty opposite cells only, fewer options on the border, and that both pieces stay indexed.

nodes.label: GameActionKeyTest
nodes.rationale: Locks actionKey round-trips, lifting targetCellId from params, and that legacy secondCellId is not the displayed cell.

nodes.label: GameStateViewJsonSerializationTest
nodes.rationale: Locks camelCase JSON, string piece ids, both ids on manipulator step 2, and a null cell on acrobat step 1.

nodes.label: GameWsExceptionHandlerTest
nodes.rationale: Locks ILLEGAL_MOVE plus the engine message, STALE_VERSION plus actualVersion, and that rejections are only for the command destination.
